claim: Someone shared a message saying Lassa fever has already killed more than 250 people in Nigeria this year and that it has reached more than twenty states.
normalizedClaim: Lassa fever has killed more than 250 people in Nigeria in 2026 and has been confirmed in more than twenty states.
explanation: The NCDC's Lassa fever situation report for epi week 34 of 2026 states that 253 deaths have been reported cumulatively, with a case fatality rate of 24.0%, and that 24 states have recorded at least one confirmed case across 118 Local Government Areas. Both parts of the claim match what that report says. The figures are cumulative for 2026 up to 23 August, so they will have moved since.
simpleExplanation: Nigeria's disease control centre reported 253 Lassa fever deaths across 24 states in 2026, up to late August. The claim matches that report.
unknowns: How many deaths have been reported since 23 August 2026, the last week this report covers.
Whether the message was describing this year or an earlier outbreak.
action: Check the NCDC situation reports page for the most recent week before repeating the figures.

claim: A voice note is going round saying the health authorities have confirmed a herbal mixture cures Lassa fever and that nobody needs to go to hospital for it any more.
normalizedClaim: Nigerian health authorities have confirmed that a herbal mixture cures Lassa fever, so hospital treatment is no longer necessary.
explanation: The NCDC's own recommendation in its Lassa fever situation report for epi week 34 of 2026 tells healthcare workers to maintain high suspicion for Lassa fever and to initiate timely referral and treatment. That is the opposite of saying hospital care is unnecessary. The same report records a case fatality rate of 24.0% for 2026, and names late presentation of cases as a reason that rate is high. Nothing in the report mentions a herbal cure.
simpleExplanation: The NCDC tells health workers to refer and treat Lassa fever cases promptly. It does not describe any herbal cure, and delay is one reason the death rate is high.
unknowns: Which group or person the voice note was attributed to.
Whether the message referred to a specific product being sold.
action: Do not share the voice note, and contact the NCDC on its toll-free line 6232 to confirm anything about Lassa fever treatment.

claim: I heard that from next week every household in my area has to pay a new waste collection fee directly to a collector who comes to the door.
normalizedClaim: Households must pay a new waste collection fee directly to a door-to-door collector from next week.
explanation: The curated store holds nothing about a door-to-door waste collection fee, and the claim does not say which state or local government area it refers to. That is not evidence the claim is false — it means Ukweli cannot check it. Absence of a record here says nothing either way about what any authority has announced.
simpleExplanation: Ukweli has no source covering this, so it cannot say whether it is true or false.
unknowns: Which state or local government area the claim refers to.
Which body is said to have authorised the fee.
Whether any official notice about this fee exists at all.
